title: Reseller Onramp — Technical & Copy Gates Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for onboarding resellers and integrators into cloud marketplace channels (AWS/Azure/GCP) where Redwood will be a listed product. Focus: the combined technical acceptance gates + tile/marketing copy checklist so marketplace PMs and channel ops can run a preflight.

High-level goals (why this doc):
- Reduce back-and-forth during marketplace ingestion by consolidating technical gating + copy approval steps.
- Provide templated copy snippets and test cases for trial provisioning + entitlement mapping.
- Surface legal/billing risks early (SAML/KMS, data residency, trial usage caps).

Quick TL;DR checklist (one-line items for standups):
- Product tile copy: title, short blurb (<=140 chars), 1–2 benefits bullets, 3 security bullets. (Owner: Rina)
- Technical acceptance: SSO, billing hookup, KMS, network egress, image provenance tests. (Owner: Diego)
- Trial flow: how trial is provisioned in marketplace vs Redwood console; test plan. (Owner: Ben)
- Legal review: data handling + indemnities for reseller distribution. (Owner: Priya)

Acceptance gate matrix (must pass all to publish):
1) Tile copy & metadata
   - Title: concise, searchable, include “Redwood Inference” or partner co-brand? decide (Rina).
   - Short description (<=140 chars): actionable benefit line. Example: "Low-latency LLM inference with predictable costs — Redwood Inference, deployable to your VPC."
   - Long description: 1–2 short paragraphs + 4 bullets (features). Keep product/partner differentiation clear.
   - Keywords/tags: AI, LLM inference, GPU, low-latency, dedicated capacity, private deployment.
   - Icons/screenshots: PNG 1200x600, no sensitive data; include console shot with mock data.

2) Technical onboarding checklist
   - SSO: test SAML OIDC SSO flow with partner test account. Provide step-by-step SSO setup doc (linked).
   - Provisioning API: marketplace must be able to call Redwood provisioning API (POST /provision) with auth token; sandbox key provided.
   - Billing integration: ensure usage meter mapping exists (tokens/embedding units -> marketplace metering SKU). Confirm rounding/fallback logic.
   - Trial provisioning: test trial creation, expiration, and conversion to paid. Edge cases: multiple trials per customer, trial credit carryover, resellers creating trials on behalf.
   - KMS/HSM: for private deployments or BYOK, verify KMS key import and decryption flow. Document proof-of-concept run.
   - Network egress/privacy: confirm permitted IP ranges, VPC peering steps (if required). List egress ports and destinations.
   - Container/image provenance: for partner-managed listings that publish an image, provide SHA256 image digest and attestations.

3) Security & compliance bullets (these show on tile and must be true)
   - SOC2 Type II (in process/obtained) — state current status.
   - Data residency options: US/EU/APAC (list regions supported).
   - Encryption: TLS in transit + KMS at rest (BYOK optional).

Sample tile copy (working drafts — pick one):
- Short title: Redwood Inference — Hosted & Private LLM Serving
- Short blurb (140 chars): Fast, predictable LLM inference: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, or private VPC deployments.
- 3 benefit bullets (for tile):
  • Predictable cost controls (batching, caching, quantization)
  • SLA-backed dedicated capacity for production throughput
  • Private deployment options for regulated data
- Security bullets (for tile):
  • SOC2-aligned controls
  • Option for BYOK via KMS
  • VPC-friendly networking

SKU & metering mapping notes
- Internal mapping: Redwood usage unit = token-generation unit; marketplace must expose SKU that maps to tokens and embeddings separately. Example mapping table attached in Confluence.
- Billing edge case: if marketplace rounds metered units, make sure to document potential 1–2% variance in Redwood reports.

Trial & UX flow (test cases)
- Launch trial through marketplace tile -> marketplace provisions trial account via provisioning API -> Redwood sends onboarding email -> user hits trial cap (e.g., 500k tokens) -> verify notifications and conversion CTA.
- Test cases: expired trial, trial extended by reseller, multiple trials merged. For each case, note expected behavior and owner to fix.

Legal & contract checkpoints (initial list, send to Legal):
- Reseller distribution addendum: who owns customer contract? (we usually prefer direct contract with customer, reseller as reseller — decide).
- Data processing addendum: if private deployment allowed, ensure DPA covers partner-managed infra.
- Indemnity and liability ceilings: propose marketplace-friendly wording.
- Trial terms & renewal: ensure marketplace trial binding language matches Redwood’s trial cancellation policy.

Known risks / unresolved questions (explicit):
- Q: Do we allow partners to co-brand tile copy? Risk: accidental brand/claim mismatch. (Action: Rina to propose co-branding guidelines)
- Q: Marketplace SKU granularity — do we split by model family (e.g., rw-1-small vs rw-1-large) or by unit type only? Ops/Finance leaning: start coarse (unit-level) then iterate. (Action: Ben + Finance)
- Q: Private deployments via marketplace — is this allowed in cloud marketplaces or must be direct contract? (Action: Legal + Platform)

Operational runbook (preflight sequence — recommended timeline):
- Day -14: Marketing copy freeze + screenshots approved. (Rina)
- Day -12: Provisioning sandbox keys and test account prepared. (Diego)
- Day -10: Billing SKU mapping confirmed with Finance and Marketplace team. (Ben)
- Day -7: Security checklist signed off by Security & Legal. (Priya)
- Day -3: Final tile uploaded to staging marketplace; smoke tests run. (All)
- Day 0: Publish to marketplace + monitor first 72h for provisioning failures, billing mismatches, and support tickets. (GTM on-call + SRE)

Support and SLAs post-launch
- Define 24/7 on-call for provisioning failures for first 72 hours.
- Escalation path: GTM -> Product -> SRE -> Legal. Include contact phone numbers in internal runbook (redacted in public tile).

Monitoring & telemetry (what to instrument before publish)
- Provisioning success/failure rates (per minute)
- Trial-to-paid conversion % (by channel)
- Average per-customer tokens/day and variance vs estimated commit
- Billing reconciliation delta (%) between marketplace reports and Redwood usage

Copy-edit checklist (for the final tile)
- No superlatives without evidence (avoid: "#1 latency" unless backed by benchmark).
- Avoid customer names or PII in screenshots.
- CTA: primary = "Get started (free trial)"; secondary = "Contact sales".

Appendix: quick snippets to copy/paste into marketplace form fields
- Long description (250–400 words): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers low-latency, high-throughput LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship with predictable costs using batching, caching, and quantization recommendations. Choose hosted API for fast onboarding, dedicated GPU pools for production throughput, or private VPC deployments when data residency and compliance matter."
- Feature bullets (4): "Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, Private VPC/on-prem options, Console observability + cost breakdowns"

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Rina: finalize tile copy and screenshots by 2024-12-05
- Diego: sandbox provisioning API + test run by 2024-12-08
- Ben: billing SKU mapping doc by 2024-12-10
- Priya: draft reseller addendum questions by 2024-12-12

Notes to self: keep this doc small and actionable. This is the single source for the preflight. Link to full acceptance test spreadsheet in Confluence (RT-1234). Expect multiple iterations with marketplace PMs — aim for 3 cycles max.

Tags for internal search: reseller-onramp, marketplace-preflight, tile-copy, provisioning-api, trial-flow

End of draft.
